findings.where: The 'coming soon' notice above the footer (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The launch notice sits on a bright red card. That red is not in the palette: it is brighter than the danger token, and it reads as an error or alert box. The rules give this block, the destination page's interior announcement, the ink night ground. A neutral 'listings coming soon' message is dressed as a failure.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker reaches the end of the guide and sees a red alarm box. They take it as 'something is broken' or 'this destination is unavailable' before reading the plain words. The brand owner would object too: the rule names the coming-soon notice as the ink announcement and keeps red for errors and sold-out states.

findings.where: 'Good for' tag pills (all twelve, desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The tags are a rainbow of fills: yellow, mint, pink-red, blue, purple, magenta and teal. Most of these are not palette colours. The rest are used against their only jobs: amber is for rewards only, a coral-like red is for CTAs only, and turquoise is for hero grounds and score chips. Each pill also has a border in a different, clashing hue, such as a yellow ring on red or a cyan ring on magenta. The colours carry no meaning, yet they look like a colour code.
findings.who_objects: A scanning backpacker would ask whether red 'Long stays' and 'Couples' are a warning, or whether green means recommended. They get no answer. The brand owner would object to colour with no job, to red and amber taken from their reserved roles, and to off-palette purples and pinks. The mismatched rings look like a rendering fault.

findings.fault: Only this heading is set in turquoise. Turquoise is a fill colour and is not cleared for type on sand. The other section headings, 'Surf' and 'Good for', are ink, so headings of the same rank get different colours for no reason.
findings.who_objects: A visitor would read the one coloured heading as special, a link, or a mistake. The brand owner would object to a raw fill colour used as text, which the rules bar.

findings.where: Top of the page, below the nav (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The destination page has no hero ground. The title and intro sit straight on the sand page ground. The rules make a destination page's top banner the loud zone, on a turquoise day ground. Here the page is flat sand from nav to footer, apart from the off-brand red box.
findings.who_objects: The brand owner would object because the page's one 'loud moment' is missing and the guide reads plain, close to the sterile look the brand names as its enemy. A visitor gets no sense of arrival at Canggu.
